stock.rule: Universe: S&P 100. Keep stocks above their 20-day average with a positive 5-day return. Rank by 5-day return, 20-day return, volume vs. 20-day average, and mentions in today's finance and AI headlines. Skip anything featured in the last 10 trading days. Mechanical, backward-looking, and not a recommendation.
stock.note: Hypothetical: buy at the open on the day featured, hold to the latest close, equal amounts, no fees or taxes. Five stocks over one week is mostly noise; judge the rule over months, not days.

stories.title: Object-Oriented Programming (OOP) in Python
stories.excerpt: Learn object-oriented programming in Python: the OOP paradigm, classes and inheritance, and how to instantiate objects from a class.
stories.lead:
Object-oriented programming (OOP) in Python helps you structure your code by grouping related data and behaviors into objects. You start by defining classes, which act as blueprints, and then create objects from them. OOP simplifies modeling real-world concepts in your programs and enables you to build systems that are more reusable and scalable.

By the end of this tutorial, you’ll understand that:

You’ll explore how to define classes, instantiate classes to create objects, and leverage inheritance to build robust systems in Python.

stories.title: Can Cloudflare CEO Matthew Prince save the web from AI?
stories.excerpt: Today, I’m talking with Matthew Prince, who is CEO of Cloudflare. This episode is part of a two-part series on the future of business. Matthew last joined us on the show about two and a half years ago, at what we thought then was a wild pivot point for the internet — and now it […]
stories.lead: Matthew last joined us on the show about two and a half years ago, at what we thought then was a wild pivot point for the internet — and now it turns out things are even wilder because of AI, and Matthew and Cloudflare are right at the center of it.

stories.title: Python Inner Functions: What Are They Good For?
stories.excerpt: Learn what a Python inner function is good for: accessing nonlocal names, building stateful closures, and writing your own decorators.
stories.lead:
Python inner functions are those you define inside other functions to access nonlocal names and bundle logic with its surrounding state. In this tutorial, you’ll learn how to create inner helper functions, build closures that retain state across calls, and implement decorators that modify the behavior or existing callables without changing the original implementation.

By the end of this tutorial, you’ll understand that:

You will now move through focused examples that feature encapsulated helpers, stateful closures, and decorator patterns, allowing you to apply each technique with confidence in real Python projects.

stories.title: Quiz: When Do You Use an Ellipsis in Python?
stories.excerpt: Test your understanding of Python's Ellipsis. Practice using three dots as a placeholder, in type hints, and in NumPy slicing.
stories.lead:
In this quiz, you’ll test your understanding of When Do You Use an Ellipsis in Python?

By working through this quiz, you’ll revisit how ... relates to the Ellipsis object, how to use three dots as a placeholder when you write stubs, what they mean in tuple and Callable type hints, and how they shorten your NumPy slicing syntax.

The quiz contains 6 questions and there is no time limit. You’ll get 1 point for each correct answer. At the end of the quiz, you’ll receive a total score. The maximum score is 100%. Good luck!

stories.title: Two mass shootings in South Africa leave 27 dead
stories.excerpt: The two attacks hours apart come as the country struggles to stop high levels of gang-related armed violence.
stories.lead:
Twenty-seven people have been killed in two mass shootings hours apart in South Africa, the latest gun violence to hit the country.

Seventeen people were killed when eight gunmen stormed a bar close to Johannesburg on Saturday evening, with 15 more injured.

In a separate shooting in the early hours of Sunday morning, 10 people were killed outside an entertainment venue in a township near Cape Town and a further 11 were injured.

stories.title: Sacha Zala, historian: 'Neutrality has become part of the Swiss identity, almost religious in nature'
stories.excerpt: On Sunday, September 27, Swiss citizens will vote for or against the 'safeguarding of neutrality' initiative championed by the far right. Zala discusses the ambiguities of this principle which, more than a doctrine of foreign policy, has become a cornerstone of national identity.

stories.title: Pope praises young people's 'energy and commitment' at huge open-air Mass in Paris
stories.excerpt: Around 700,000 people gathered in central Paris to hear the Catholic leader speak and offer prayer.
stories.lead:
Watch: Huge crowds greeted the Pope as he travelled down the Champs-Élysées

Pope Leo XIV has praised the "enthusiasm, energy and commitment" young people bring to the Catholic Church as dense crowds attended an open-air Mass in Paris.

An estimated 700,000 people had gathered for the Mass celebrated by the Pope from a special altar on the Place de la Concorde, on the second day of his four-day visit to France.

stories.title: Trump gave Xi Jinping a warm welcome. What did the talks accomplish?
stories.excerpt: From the National Archives to the state dinner, President Trump and Xi Jinping looked comfortable together in Washington. Two former NPR China correspondents on what the visit did and didn't deliver.
stories.lead: President Xi of China loves to win. Donald Trump loves a winner. This week, the U.S. president hosted his Chinese counterpart for nearly two days of pageantry and ritual. But did either side make any real gains? China is arguably the most consequential and difficult geopolitical relationship that the U.S. has. So to unpack the visit, we have with us NPR White House correspondent Emily Feng and NPR's Rob Schmitz, both of whom have reported extensively on China.

stories.title: Trump calls Iranian plan to reopen Strait of Hormuz not 'acceptable'
stories.excerpt: President Trump said he was rejecting an Iranian plan to reopen the Strait of Hormuz. The Iranian proposal is similar to a memorandum of understanding agreed upon by the U.S. and Iran back in June.
stories.lead:
President Trump said on Saturday that he was rejecting an Iranian plan to reopen the Strait of Hormuz.

Trump said the deal "would not be acceptable," speaking to reporters as he was departing the White House, without giving further explanation.

"I like making a deal too," he said. "But, I'm not — that deal would not be acceptable."

stories.title: Baby bank's urgent appeal as demand for help grows
stories.excerpt: The founder of Leeds Baby Bank says the charity has seen a "massive" increase in referrals recently.
stories.lead:
Chantal Nogbou founded Leeds Baby Bank in 2017 and the charity marks its first decade in January

The founder of a charity which provides essentials like Moses baskets, prams, nappies and clothes to struggling families across Leeds has said it urgently needs more donations to help keep up with demand.

Chantal Nogbou said there had been a "massive increase" in the number of people referred by health and social care professionals to Leeds Baby Bank in recent months.

stories.title: The ecstasy of buying our first home was short-lived after we found 150 faults
stories.excerpt: Getting the keys to a new home felt like a dream come true, until this couple found 150 faults.
stories.lead:
It was the day Georgina and Charles Barnes had waited three years for, as they picked up the keys to their first home.

But when the brand new property was inspected days later by a Welsh snagging company, the final quality check by independent inspectors, they found 150 defects.

These included incorrectly installed fire barriers, signs of a previous leak and what they called "exceptionally poor" workmanship.

stories.title: Nor'easter brings flooding as New York and New Jersey declare emergency
stories.excerpt: Tens of millions of people from Maine to Virginia are in the path of the powerful storm.
stories.lead:
Watch: Huge waves pummel northeast US as storm barrels through

Tens of millions of people across the north-eastern US are in the path of a powerful storm bringing coastal flooding, power cuts, travel chaos and cancelled stadium events.

The so-called nor'easter is bringing "dangerous coastal flooding and beach conditions, strong winds and heavy rainfall" to areas including New York City and Boston on Saturday, the US National Weather Service (NWS) said.

stories.title: Verani takes second successive victory as Tarasiewicz returns to winning ways at European Aquatics Open Water Swimming Cup stop in Razanac
stories.excerpt: Italy’s Dario Verani produced a stunning finish to claim his second victory in as many legs at the Razanac stop of the European Aquatics Open Water Swimming Cup 2026, powering through the final ten metres to touch ahead of Mexico’s Paolo Strehlke Delgado, who had led for the majority of the race as…
stories.lead: Verani had not led outright at any checkpoint throughout the 10km course, sitting as low as 13th after the first lap before working his way steadily through the field. He was up to fourth with just one lap remaining, then found another gear entirely on the run to the wall, catching and passing Strehlke Delgado right on the touch to win in 1:52:19.51, just 0.14 seconds clear.
